purpose: Controlled diagnosis of overshoot/direction error, alias-path and high-component phase arrangement. Exploratory fixed finite synthetic design, not predictor validation or natural-image causal identification. No matching training.
phases: one phase-aligned high branch (0,0,0), three fixed independent uniform high-branch phases; same phase vectors across templates, low branch initial phases zero
operator: Periodic separable torch bicubicAA align_cornersFalse linear M16x64 from three-period HR basis; y=M x M.T. M checked against direct tiled two-dimensional interpolation. No clipping anywhere. Original training nonperiodic bicubic and actual LR padding differ; report distribution restriction.
intervention: For supra-Nyquist templates fixed target x=.5+xL+xH, observe A(.5+xL)+eta*A(xH). eta0 blocks high-branch alias path, eta1 full operator. Low-frequency sham always observes full x for every eta; identical inputs/predictions cached but all conditions scored. Removing alias can also remove useful signal: causal contrast is the whole specified input path, not isolated internal neural mechanism.
freeze: All generated inputs, targets, M, phase vectors, protocol/source/checkpoint/source-SHA frozen before inference. Predictor reads observations only. All output cohort SHA frozen before score reads targets. Fixed deterministic diagnostic, not blinded unseen data.

evaluation.bands: fullRGB/DC included; three Chebyshev FFT bands [0,.125),[.125,.25),[.25,.5001), DC excluded. All modes even, exactly on full and center ROI FFT grids. Raw outputs and RGB averages of square error; same monochrome target in3channels.
evaluation.decomposition: d=Fc-F0; a=mean((t-F0)*d); b=mean(d*d); G=2a-b; lambda_star=a/b only b>epsilon. Harm G<-epsilon_gain: a<-epsilon_alignment wrong_direction; a>epsilon_alignment overshoot; else near_direction_boundary. Retain tiny-change/ties. Exact output-mixture diagnostic, not cell or parameter intervention.
evaluation.outcomes: every row gain,a,b,oraclelambda,cosalignment,MSE; eta1-eta0 and eta.5 contrasts within same target/phase/shift/template/model/band; phase ranges and signs within eta/shift; eta-by-phase interactions; loss weighted category and counts; no result-driven feature threshold search
evaluation.uncertainty: finite grid exhaustive descriptive counts and ranges, no independence or population CI for related modes/phases/shifts; all family/shift/model strata retained. No all-or-nothing deployment gate; unsupported results retained as boundaries.
evaluation.effect_resolution: raw abs gain<=1e-8 ties; sign flips only both sides resolved. Report continuous effects irrespective of threshold; numerical audit checks exact identities and source/target spectrum/alias controls.
evaluation.input_statistics: Save input mean/variance/periodic gradient and high-path energy for every condition; eta changes these jointly, not an alias-only effect independent of input statistics.
evaluation.interactions: Explicit [G(eta1,phasej)-G(eta0,phasej)]-[G(eta1,phase0)-G(eta0,phase0)] within same template/shift/model/ROI/band, alongside alignment and energy components.

counts.unique_observation_note: Upper bound by construction; observed exact array hashes determine cache. All supra eta0 share only4shift observations across templates/phases. All240 conditions scored; no independence claim.

budget.resume: never extend deadline; preserve failures; any source edit after first run freezes new version/root

limitations: synthetic finite modes and one checkpoint each, no natural-image prevalence/generalization
target changes with phase while amplitude spectrum stays fixed; target invariant only within eta pair
spatial translation is a linear phase ramp; shifts nested within pattern, not another independent phase cause
zero cell may be OOD; exact output mixture not evidence a cell change implements attenuation
eta0 high phase variants share the same observation, output must match; differences in truth score reflect lost information, not input-driven neural adaptation
No matching training, no new network, no old test rescoring
